issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch: The problem statement and UML require a SealSaloon constructor that accepts a String (SealSaloon(String)), but the provided example Main in the template uses a no-argument constructor (new SealSaloon()), and the solution implementation defines only a no-arg constructor (public SealSaloon()). This inconsistency will confuse students about which constructor signature to implement and may cause compilation/runtime mismatches between student code and provided examples/tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirement consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) update the problem statement and UML to require a no-argument SealSaloon() constructor (and adapt description that mentions a name), or (B) change the template Main example and the solution SealSaloon to provide and use SealSaloon(String name) and store the name if required. Ensure all provided examples, tests, and the UML match the chosen constructor signature.

issues.description: Conflicting guidance about the stock attribute initialization: the problem text instructs that orders and the stock should be initialized to default values in the SealSaloon constructor, but it also explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static (shared) and final. Initializing a static final stock in the instance constructor is contradictory or confusing. The solution initializes the static final stock at declaration, which differs from the 'initialize in constructor' guidance in the problem statement.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the intended design in the problem statement: explicitly state whether stock is an instance field initialized in the constructor or a static (class-level) final field initialized at declaration. If stock should be shared across instances, keep it static final and update the problem text to say it should be initialized at declaration (or in a static initializer). If it should be per-instance, remove the static requirement. Make the initialization instruction match the chosen design.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML explicitly specify a constructor SealSaloon(String) (a saloon name parameter) but the provided solution implements a no-argument constructor SealSaloon(). This mismatch between the documented constructor signature and the implemented constructor can confuse students about how to instantiate the SealSaloon and whether they must provide a name parameter. The template's example Main also uses new SealSaloon() (no-arg), which further conflicts with the textual requirement that the constructor takes a String. Students may waste time reconciling the UML/text with the code or may implement an incorrect constructor signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the constructor signature across artifacts. Either update the solution (and template examples) to provide a public SealSaloon(String name) constructor (and add a corresponding private name field with getter) or change the problem statement/UML to require a no-argument constructor. Prefer implementing public SealSaloon(String name) to match the documented requirement.
